meta.siteQueryNote: The live site's web app reads ?q= and fills in the search box (web/app.js syncFromUrl); results may differ from the saved offline runs.

queries.generator: Queries were written by gemma-4-31b-it from source papers (queries.jsonl model field).

judgments.description: AI-graded, not human-validated: GPT-5.4 mini 0/1/2 grades with 100 ASTRA reference overrides, plus a top-20 completion layer of additional AI grades (arxiv-search README, 'Relevance labels').

originalSnapshot.note: Every one of its grades is unchanged in the 3,678-pair pool (checked by this script).

bm25.label: Keyword baseline (BM25)
bm25.description: Tuned BM25 over titles (counted twice), abstracts and authors, exact terms plus stems, k1=0.8, b=0.75.

reranker.label: AI reranker
reranker.description: Hybrid BM25 + OpenAI-embedding retrieval (Decision 36); two GPT-5.4 mini passes over the top 50, fused with retrieval order (Decision 46); then two GPT-5.4 passes re-score the top 20, ordered by the average score, keeping rank 1 (Decision 50).

meta.caveat: Both nDCG@10 numbers use the same 100 dev queries but different judgment pools (3,294 vs 3,678), so the change is not a like-for-like gain. Settings were tuned on these queries, so scores are optimistic.

samePoolNdcg10.note: Recomputed by this script from the saved runs; not a published project number.

metric.name: nDCG@5
metric.ideal: the same 5 papers sorted by grade

selection.queries: Six dev queries hand-picked for plain wording, a grade-2 and a grade-0 candidate, and different system orders.
selection.candidates: Alternate between the BM25 run and the reranker run, BM25 first, each time taking that system's highest-ranked judged paper not already chosen, until 5 papers.
selection.systemOrder: Each system's order is its own rank of the 5 papers in its saved run; papers missing from its saved top 100 go last, in ascending arXiv-id order.
selection.start: Seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle (FNV-1a of `<queryId>#<attempt>` into mulberry32); the first attempt that differs from both system orders and whose nDCG@5 (to 3 decimals) is no higher than either system's is used, so an unchanged submission never wins.

paperMetadata.snippet: First sentence of the abstract, or its first 28 words, when the abstract is longer than 30 words.
